body:
> Observed 2026-08-28 on pipao-v2, an adopter whose maintainer also works from a machine with only pipao checked out. The adopter's own answer to "where is hkb" is already local: `.agents/skills/kanban/scripts/hkb` does `command -v hkb || npx -y hkb-cli`, and `npx hkb …` resolves `node_modules/.bin` first. What broke was the one thing that cannot go through npx: the hooks.

## Why

`npm i -D hkb-cli` is the proper adopter install — the version is pinned in `package.json`/lockfile, every machine and every teammate gets it from `npm install`, no global step, no PATH drift when nvm's `lts/*` alias moves. hkb does not support it today:

- Claude Code runs hook commands in a plain `/bin/sh` with the session's PATH; `node_modules/.bin` is not on it. So the bare `hkb hook <verb>` init writes fails on every tool call in every session (`/bin/sh: 1: hkb: not found`), and the hooks are the only thing the repo's other sessions ever see of hkb.
- `hkbOnPath()` (`src/board.js:164`) is wrong under `npx hkb init`: npx puts `node_modules/.bin` on the child's PATH, so init answers "on PATH", writes the bare form, and it never resolves outside npx. Run as `./node_modules/.bin/hkb init` it writes `node "/abs/path/to/repo/node_modules/hkb-cli/bin/hkb.js"` into `settings.local.json` — right on this machine, meaningless on the next, so `init` has to be repeated per machine (#85's compromise, which a local install no longer needs).
- Claude Code sets `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` for hook commands precisely so a project can reference its own files portably. `node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/node_modules/hkb-cli/bin/hkb.js" hook stop` is the same on every machine that ran `npm install` — it belongs in the **tracked** `.claude/settings.json`, and then a teammate's `git pull && npm install` is the whole setup.

## What

1. **Detect the local install** (`src/init.js`, pure helper in `src/model.js`): `PKG_ROOT` sits under `<repo>/node_modules/` — compare against the repo root, not PATH. `hkbCommandForHook` gains this case and returns `node "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/node_modules/hkb-cli/bin/hkb.js" hook <verb>` (the package name from `package.json`, never hard-coded). Treat it as **portable** (`isPortableHookCommand`): it means the same on every machine, so `hookPlacement` puts it in the tracked file by default, no `--shared-hooks` needed. Fix `hkbOnPath()` so npx's augmented PATH does not count — strip `node_modules/.bin` entries, or resolve `command -v hkb` and reject a path under the repo's `node_modules`.
2. **Worktree edge.** A worker runs in `.claude/worktrees/kb-<n>-<k>`, a fresh checkout with no `node_modules` until it runs `npm ci`; `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` there is the worktree. Both hooks are inert without `KB_TASK`, so the command guards: `f="$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/node_modules/hkb-cli/bin/hkb.js"; [ -f "$f" ] || exit 0; exec node "$f" hook <verb>` — one line, no output, no error before the install; the Stop hook is what matters and by then `npm ci` has run. Say in `docs/harnesses.md` that a worker prompt on a local-install board should install before it finishes. (#144 later hands the worker the absolute path of the hkb that ran the dispatcher, which closes this fully.)
3. **`hkb doctor`** (`checkHooks`, `hookCommandNeeds`): understand the guarded form; resolve `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` to the repo root when checking that the file exists; on a local install where the tracked file still holds the bare `hkb` form, say so with the fix (`hkb init` rewrites it). `hookCommandNeeds` currently tokenises the first two words — extend it, do not special-case.
4. **The skill shim** (`skills/kanban/scripts/hkb`): keep it; it is already right for a local install. One comment saying so.
5. **Docs**: README's install section names `npm i -D hkb-cli` + `npx hkb init` as the adopter path and `npm i -g` as the alternative; `docs/harnesses.md` hooks table gets the local-install row; `src/init.js` header comment (#85's reasoning) gets the third case; wiki page covering hooks (`docs/wiki/architecture/overview.md`; run `node .repolore/scripts/wiki-check.mjs`).

## Done when

- In a repo with `hkb-cli` in `devDependencies`, `npx hkb init` writes the `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` form into `.claude/settings.json`, and a second machine that runs `git pull && npm install` has working hooks with no further command.
- No session in that repo logs a hook error, installed or not: before `npm install` the hook exits 0 silently.
- `npx hkb doctor` on that repo reports `✓ hook command` with the file it resolved, and a stale bare-`hkb` entry as a failure naming `hkb init`.
- Tests: `hkbCommandForHook` for the local case, `hkbOnPath` ignoring `node_modules/.bin`, `hookPlacement` treating the form as portable, `hookCommandNeeds` parsing the guarded form (`test/harness.test.js`, `test/doctor.test.js`). `npm run lint && npm test` green; `npm run smoke` (init output changed) — and the smoke's scratch repo should exercise the local-install branch.

## Contract

- Blocks #144: both edit `hkbCommandForHook`, `checkHooks` and the same docs; #144 branches from this merge.
- Do not remove the global-install path or `--shared-hooks`; this adds the third case, it does not replace the first two.
- No new dependency; the detection is a path comparison.
goal: An adopter installs hkb-cli as a devDependency and runs npx hkb init once: the hooks land in the tracked .claude/settings.json as a CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR-relative command that resolves on every machine after npm install, exits 0 silently before it, and hkb doctor verifies it
title: Support npm i -D hkb-cli: init writes a $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR-relative hook command into the tracked settings
